name: Core 2031 — Mixed Roles
description: Sales, Engineering and Leadership hiring at a fast-growing Noida SaaS company.

rounds.title: Junior Sales Executive
brief: Good morning, Recruiter. I'm ARIA, your AI shortlisting agent. 🛰️
First up: a Junior Sales Executive for our inside-sales pod. 1–2 years of B2B calling, CRM hygiene, and grit. Budget ₹4–6 LPA.
I've ranked 6 candidates. I'm usually right… usually. Swipe ⭐ to shortlist, 🚩 to flag a red flag, ➡️ to skip. You make the call.
rounds.rookie_tip: Tip: compare the dates on each CV. Two full-time jobs can't run at the same time.

questions.text: Walk me through last month's numbers — dials, meetings booked, deals closed.
Tell me about a deal you expected to win and lost. What did you change after?
What are your biggest strengths and weaknesses?
Walk me through your timeline month by month since 2029 — any overlaps or gaps?
How did you get along with your last manager and team?

rounds.aria_mistake: ARIA got this one right — Priya's numbers are real and specific. But ARIA also scored Sneha 10 points above Faiz purely on college tier, and rated Arjun 82 without noticing that his two 'full-time' jobs overlap by 7 months.
rounds.best_hire_explanation: Priya combines verifiable activity metrics (60 dials/day, 14 meetings/month) with a learning mindset after lost deals. Clean CV, realistic salary, short notice.

candidates.name: Priya Nair
candidates.title: Business Development Rep, Cloudkart Solutions
candidates.aria_reason: Consistent quota attainment language and strong CRM keywords.

lines: “I average about 60 dials a day; last month that became 14 qualified meetings and 3 closures.”
“When a deal stalls I go back to discovery — usually I skipped a stakeholder.”

details.activity: Active on ScriniLink 2 days ago · applied directly

candidates.suspicion: 5-month gap between internship and first job

q1.text: “Dials: ~1,250. Meetings booked: 14. Closed: 3 at an average ₹1.8L ACV. I can share my CRM dashboard screenshot.”

q2.text: “Lost a logistics client to a cheaper tool. I'd never met their finance head. Now I map every decision-maker in week one.”

q5.text: “No overlaps. The 5-month gap in 2029 was when my father had surgery — I did a Sales Navigator certification online during that time.”
q5.clears: The gap was caregiving + upskilling. Not a red flag.

candidates.reference_quote: “Priya books more meetings than anyone in her batch and updates the CRM the same day. I'd rehire her.” — Team Lead, Cloudkart
candidates.hire_outcome: Six months in: 118% of quota, now mentoring the next intern batch.

candidates.name: Arjun Mehta
candidates.title: Sales Executive, Ventro Telecom
candidates.aria_reason: 3 sales roles, Salesforce + negotiation keywords, continuous employment.

lines: “I've handled both telecom and B2B ecommerce clients.”
“I'm a closer — my targets were always met.”

flags.explanation: Ventro Telecom (Mar 2030–present) overlaps with a full-time role at Quickmart B2B (Aug 2029–Oct 2030) by 7 months. Two full-time jobs can't run in parallel — one of them is padded.

q5.text: “Uh… Quickmart ended earlier actually, I just didn't update the date. Or it was part-time for some months.”

q1.text: “I don't remember exact numbers, but I always hit target.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Arjun was with us for about 4 months in 2030, not a year. He left without serving notice.” — HR, Quickmart B2B
candidates.hire_outcome: Background verification failed in month 2 — offer revoked, role reopened.

candidates.name: Sneha Kulkarni
candidates.title: Inside Sales Associate, Fintrail Payments
candidates.aria_reason: Tier-1 institute, relevant fintech sales experience.

lines: “I run 3 email sequences a week and follow up by phone within 24 hours.”
“My meeting-to-demo rate is around 40%.”

q1.text: “About 900 dials, 10 meetings, 2 closures. Fintech cycles are longer, so I track demos more.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Reliable, organised, good with follow-ups. Solid performer.” — Manager, Fintrail
candidates.hire_outcome: Steady performer — 94% of quota at six months.

candidates.name: Mohammed Faiz
candidates.title: Inside Sales Associate, Paysetu Fintech
candidates.aria_reason: Relevant fintech sales; institute ranked lower in pedigree index.

lines: “I run 3 email sequences a week and follow up by phone within 24 hours.”
“My meeting-to-demo rate is close to 40%.”

q1.text: “Roughly 900 dials, 10 meetings, 2 closures. Fintech has longer cycles so I track demos closely.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Reliable, organised, great with follow-ups. Solid performer.” — Manager, Paysetu
candidates.hire_outcome: Steady performer — 95% of quota at six months.

candidates.name: Rahul Verma
candidates.title: Senior Sales Associate, Dealhive
candidates.aria_reason: Top-quartile revenue numbers, ‘Senior’ title, closing keywords.

lines: “I was the top closer — honestly the rest of the team just slowed me down.”
“My last manager didn't understand sales, so I mostly worked around him.”

details.references: Prefers not to share current manager

flags.explanation: Blames team and manager in the interview, avoids giving a manager reference, and treats colleagues as obstacles. High individual numbers, high team-damage risk.

q6.text: “Honestly, my managers have never been very good. I perform better when nobody micromanages me and the team doesn't drag me down.”

q2.text: “I don't really lose deals. When I do it's because pre-sales messed up the demo.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Strong closer, but two juniors asked to be moved off his pod.” — Former peer, Urbanstack
candidates.hire_outcome: Hit target for 2 quarters; 2 team members resigned citing him. Exited in month 8.

candidates.name: Kavya Reddy
candidates.title: Sales Associate, Spicewell D2C

lines: “I can join in 15 days, my company is flexible.”
“Currently I'm at around 6 LPA.”

flags.explanation: Interview says 15-day notice and ₹6 LPA current pay; application form says 90-day notice and ₹3.6 LPA CTC. Expectation of ₹7.5 LPA is ~2x current and above budget.

q5.text: “Spicewell since Feb 2030. Notice is… I think 90 days officially, but they might release me early.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Kavya is good with customers. Notice is 90 days, no buyout.” — Supervisor, Spicewell
candidates.hire_outcome: Accepted, then joined a competitor on the day of joining.

rounds.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
brief: Round 2: a Senior Full-Stack Engineer (React + Node + cloud) for the core platform team. Budget ₹28–38 LPA.
Engineering CVs are where keyword stuffing lives. I've matched against 412 skill tokens.
My #1 pick scored 94. Do you agree? Use the interview question to test claims, not to make small talk.
rounds.rookie_tip: Tip: a high ARIA score can come from keywords alone. Look for proof of hands-on work.

questions.text: Pick a production incident you owned end-to-end. What broke and what did you change?
On Kubernetes — what exactly did you configure yourself? Walk me through a manifest.
Walk me through 2019–2021 — who did you report to at each company?
As VP, how big was the team you led and what did you ship?
Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
Tell me about your career break and how you kept your skills current.

rounds.aria_mistake: ARIA scored Rohan 94 because his CV matched 38 of 40 keywords — but the keywords were copied from the JD, and his 2019–2021 roles at Nexacore and Bluefin Labs overlap by 18 months. ARIA also docked Meera 12 points for a caregiving gap that has nothing to do with her skills.
rounds.best_hire_explanation: Ananya's CV undersells her: 2 production incident write-ups, open-source contributions and a clean timeline. ARIA ranked her #4 because her CV uses plain language instead of buzzwords.

candidates.name: Rohan Malhotra
candidates.title: Principal Full-Stack Architect, Nexacore
candidates.education: B.Tech CSE, Western Ghats Institute of Technology (Tier 1), 2015
candidates.aria_reason: 38/40 JD keyword match, 'Principal Architect' seniority, full cloud stack.

lines: “I've architected solutions across the full stack using best-in-class paradigms.”
“At Nexacore we leveraged synergies between microservices and AI.”

flags.explanation: Nexacore (Jun 2019–present) and Bluefin Labs (Jan 2018–Feb 2021) overlap by ~20 months as two full-time senior roles.
Lists 5 frontend frameworks, 5 languages, 3 clouds and Blockchain — near-verbatim from our JD. The interview is all buzzwords and no specifics.

q3.text: “At Bluefin I was more of a… consultant towards the end. I'd have to check the dates. I reported to various stakeholders.”

q1.text: “We had a latency issue and I architected a holistic solution using caching paradigms.” (No specifics after two follow-ups.)

q2.text: “I oversaw the Kubernetes strategy at a high level.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Rohan left Bluefin in mid-2019. We have no record of employment after that.” — HR, Bluefin Labs
candidates.hire_outcome: Couldn't ship a single feature unassisted in 90 days. Exit + rehire cost ≈ ₹18L.

candidates.name: Daniel Fernandes
candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer, Orbitpay
candidates.education: B.E. IT, Goa Coastal Engineering College (Tier 2), 2021

lines: “Our DevOps team handled the cluster, I mostly pushed to the pipeline.”
“System design — I've read a lot about it, we followed the architect's diagrams.”

flags.explanation: CV headlines Kubernetes and system design, but the interview shows he consumed both — DevOps owned the cluster and an architect owned the design. A solid mid-level React/Node dev, not a senior owner.

q2.text: “I haven't written manifests myself — DevOps gave us a Helm chart template. I just changed the image tag.”

q1.text: “A payment retry bug — I fixed the React form validation. The infra side was handled by SRE.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Good React dev, dependable. Wouldn't put him on infra or design reviews yet.” — Tech Lead, Orbitpay
candidates.hire_outcome: Good feature dev, but the platform team still needed a senior infra owner — a second hire was required.

candidates.name: Kunal Bansal
candidates.title: VP of Engineering, Snackr (stealth)
candidates.aria_reason: VP + CTO titles indicate leadership seniority.

lines: “As VP I set the engineering vision.”
“I'm looking for a senior IC role now, to go deeper technically.”

flags.explanation: 'VP of Engineering' at a 5-person company with ~4 years of total experience. He led 1 other engineer. The title doesn't mean senior scope.

q4.text: “The team was me and one intern, plus a freelance designer. We shipped an MVP app.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Kunal's a hustler. Title was more of a startup thing, honestly.” — Founder, Snackr
candidates.hire_outcome: Energetic, but performed at mid-level. Expected a 'Head of' title within 6 months.

candidates.name: Ananya Iyer
candidates.title: Software Engineer III, Lumen Health Tech
candidates.education: B.Tech CSE, Kaveri Regional Engineering College (Tier 2), 2022
candidates.aria_reason: Relevant stack; fewer leadership and architecture keywords.

lines: “I wrote the post-mortem when our appointment API went down — root cause was a connection pool leak.”
“I maintain a small open-source date library, ~2k stars.”

q1.text: “Pool exhaustion under load. I added pool metrics, a circuit breaker, and a load test in CI. p99 went from 4s to 300ms.”
q1.clears: Plain CV wording hid real senior ownership — confirmed.

q2.text: “We're on ECS, not K8s. I've done K8s in side projects — I'd ramp up but I won't pretend I've run it in prod.”
q2.clears: Honest about gaps — a positive signal.

candidates.reference_quote: “Ananya is the person we call at 2am. Quietly the strongest engineer on the team.” — EM, Lumen Health Tech
candidates.hire_outcome: Led the platform migration in month 5; now the go-to reviewer for the backend.

candidates.name: Meera Joshi
candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer (returning)
candidates.education: B.Tech IT, Narmada Institute of Technology (Tier 2), 2019

lines: “I shipped checkout for Peregrine — 3M orders a month.”
“During the break I rebuilt my portfolio on the current React and Node versions.”

details.references: Former EM at Peregrine + 2 freelance clients

q6.text: “Caring for my mother after a stroke. I kept a weekly build log, did 2 freelance projects on React 22 and Node 30.”
q6.clears: Gap was caregiving; skills are current. Not a red flag.

q1.text: “A cart-total rounding bug under a sale spike. I added property-based tests and a reconciliation job.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Meera owned checkout end-to-end. I'd hire her back tomorrow.” — Former EM, Peregrine
candidates.hire_outcome: Strong senior IC — owned the payments module by month 4.

candidates.name: Vikram Singh
candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer, Coralbay Commerce
candidates.education: B.Tech IT, Narmada Institute of Technology (Tier 2), 2021

lines: “I shipped the checkout flow at Coralbay — ~3M orders a month.”
“I keep up with the latest React and Node releases through side projects.”

q1.text: “A cart-total rounding bug during a sale. I added property-based tests and a nightly reconciliation job.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Vikram owns checkout end-to-end. Strong hire.” — EM, Coralbay
candidates.hire_outcome: Strong senior IC — owned the payments module by month 4.

rounds.title: Head of Operations
brief: Final round: Head of Operations — 300+ people across 3 sites. Budget ₹55–75 LPA. A bad hire here costs ~₹45L.
Leadership CVs are polished. Red flags hide in tone, tenure maths and numbers that don't add up.
Optional: Blind Mode hides names, photos, age and institutes so you judge only the evidence.
rounds.rookie_tip: Tip: check if the years of leadership add up to the graduation year, and listen to how people talk about their teams.

questions.text: Walk me through a cost-reduction programme you led: baseline, levers, result, and who owned what.
Tell me about a time your team missed a major target. What did you do?
Map each leadership role to your graduation year and explain every move.
Describe a DMAIC project you ran — what was the defect metric and the control plan?
Why do you want to join us?
Confirm your notice period and current CTC for the offer letter.

rounds.aria_mistake: ARIA scored Natasha 94 because her CV hits every leadership keyword ('transformation', 'P&L', 'scale'). But her interview language is dismissive of her teams and her notice/CTC numbers change between documents. ARIA also rated Karan 9 points above Rajesh — an identical profile — because Rajesh graduated 18 years earlier.
rounds.best_hire_explanation: Farah's results are specific and attributed to her team (₹11Cr savings, 23% SLA improvement) and her job moves were all acquisitions. ARIA under-scored her because of 'frequent job changes'.

candidates.name: Natasha Kapoor
candidates.title: VP Operations, Stratus Mobility
candidates.aria_reason: Full leadership keyword coverage: transformation, P&L, scale-up, Tier-1 MBA.

lines: “I turned around operations that my predecessors — and frankly my team — had run into the ground.”
“I don't tolerate excuses. People either keep up or they're out.”

details.references: Board member at Stratus (not direct manager)

flags.explanation: Takes credit for turnarounds and blames predecessors and her own team; 'people keep up or they're out' signals high attrition risk for a 300-person org.
Notice period is 30 days in the interview and 90 days on the form; her ₹85 LPA ask is 47% above current and above the ₹75 LPA cap.

q2.text: “Missed target? That happened under my predecessor. When my team misses, I replace the weak links. I let go of 40% of the leads in year one.”

q6.text: “Current is around 72 fixed… well, 58 fixed plus variable. Notice is 90 days but I can negotiate.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Delivers numbers. Attrition in her org was 3x company average.” — Former HRBP, Trellis
candidates.hire_outcome: Cut costs 8% in Q1; 3 site leads resigned by month 5; exited in month 11. Total cost ≈ ₹45L.

candidates.name: Vivek Choudhary
candidates.title: Head of Operations, Ganga Fresh Retail
candidates.aria_reason: Two Head of Ops roles; '12+ years' and '400+ team' keywords.

lines: “I've been leading operations for more than 12 years.”
“At Swiftcart I built the ops team from zero to 400.”

flags.explanation: Claims '12+ years of ops leadership' but graduated in 2018 — that's at most ~13 years of total work, and he was a fresher manager in 2019. Head of Ops at 27 for a 400-person org is implausible.
Swiftcart Express was a 40-person delivery startup during his tenure; 'Head of Operations' meant running one hub.

q3.text: “Well — 12 years including internships and family business. Swiftcart was smaller when I joined… maybe 40 people. The 400 includes delivery partners.”

q1.text: “We reduced costs a lot, maybe 20–30%. The finance team has the exact numbers.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Vivek ran our Noida hub, about 35 people. Good on the floor.” — Former COO, Swiftcart
candidates.hire_outcome: Strong floor manager, but out of depth at 300+ scale. Needed a COO hire above him.

candidates.name: Lakshmi Menon
candidates.title: Director, Business Excellence, Coastline Pharma
candidates.education: M.Tech Industrial Eng., Southern Institute of Technology (Tier 1), 2012
candidates.aria_reason: Black Belt certification + full process-excellence keyword set.

lines: “I've championed a culture of continuous improvement across the enterprise.”
“My philosophy is that quality is everyone's responsibility.”

flags.explanation: Claims Black Belt + DMAIC, but can't name a defect metric, baseline or control plan for any project. The certification was a 5-day online course; her work was training delivery, not running ops.
Skills list is a glossary of process terms; interview answers are slogans with no numbers.

q4.text: “DMAIC is Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control. We applied it across functions to drive a quality mindset.” (No metric, no project named.)

q1.text: “I enabled teams through Kaizen workshops. The savings were realised by the business units.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Lakshmi delivered our Six Sigma training programme to 200 staff.” — L&D Head, Malabar Healthcare
candidates.hire_outcome: Great trainer; struggled to run day-to-day operations. Moved to an L&D role in month 7.

candidates.name: Karan Arora
candidates.title: Senior Director, Operations, Nimbus Foods
candidates.education: MBA Operations, Aravalli School of Management (Tier 2), 2020
candidates.aria_reason: Multi-site ops, recent leadership, high trajectory.

lines: “My team cut cost-per-order by 14% in 18 months — mostly by redesigning shift rosters.”
“I spend a third of my week coaching site leads.”

q1.text: “Baseline ₹38/order. Levers: roster redesign, vendor consolidation. Result ₹32.7/order. Site leads owned the rollout.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Karan builds leaders under him. Reliable through peak season.” — CEO, Nimbus Foods
candidates.hire_outcome: Solid leader; sites stable, cost targets met.

candidates.name: Farah Siddiqui
candidates.title: Head of Operations, Tessellate Health
candidates.aria_reason: Relevant scale; 3 employers in 5 years lowers stability score.

lines: “My team took ₹11 crore out of the cost base and improved SLA adherence by 23%.”
“The credit goes to four site leads I hired and coached.”

q3.text: “2016 MBA. Labnest was acquired by Medipath in 2027, then Medipath by Tessellate in 2029 — I moved with each acquisition and integrated the teams.”
q3.clears: 'Job hopping' was two acquisitions. Stable, not a flight risk.

q1.text: “Baseline ₹96Cr ops cost. Levers: lab routing, reagent contracts, shift design. ₹11Cr saved, audited by finance. Site leads owned execution.”

q2.text: “We missed a turnaround-time SLA in monsoon 2030. I owned it publicly, rebuilt courier routing with the team, and we recovered in 6 weeks.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Farah is the reason the merger didn't fall apart. Her team would follow her anywhere.” — CEO, Tessellate Health
candidates.hire_outcome: Integrated 2 new sites in 6 months; attrition down 30%; promoted to COO track.

candidates.name: Rajesh Pillai
candidates.title: Senior Director, Operations, Coastal Kitchens
candidates.education: MBA Operations, Aravalli School of Management (Tier 2), 2002
candidates.aria_reason: Relevant multi-site ops; older graduation year reduces 'growth trajectory' score.

lines: “My team cut cost-per-order by 14% in 18 months — mostly by redesigning shift rosters.”
“I spend a third of my week coaching site leads.”

details.references: CEO at Coastal Kitchens + former reportee

q1.text: “Baseline ₹38/order. Levers: roster redesign, vendor consolidation. Result ₹32.7/order. Site leads owned the rollout.”

candidates.reference_quote: “Rajesh builds leaders under him. Reliable through peak season.” — CEO, Coastal Kitchens
candidates.hire_outcome: Solid leader; sites stable, cost targets met.
